subject: PoC / Trial plan & deployment mode next steps (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: PoC follow-up: deployment mode preferences and next steps

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the call today — really helpful to hear more about Acme's inferencing needs for the Assistant project. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align the PoC: 

Call recap (high level):
- Primary constraint: data residency and strict audit controls for PII / customer data.
- Workload: primarily multi-turn chat and classification for support tickets (~300 RPS peak, avg 1.2k tokens/session).
- Success criteria: latency P95 goal < 150ms, consistent output quality vs current baseline, and integration with Acme's SSO/KMS.

Deployment modes discussed:
1) Hosted API — fastest to start and lowest engineering lift; suitable if Acme can route only non-sensitive traffic or if token-level PII is stripped before sending.
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pool in our cloud; gives separation of traffic and predictable throughput; recommended if you need performance guarantees but don't want full on-prem.
3) Private VPC / on-prem — full data control (VPC peering or air-gapped on-prem); best for regulated data and strict audit logs.

From our conversation it sounded like Acme will likely prefer Private VPC, with Dedicated as a fallback if timelines or hardware procurement push back on-prem.

Proposed PoC (draft):
- Scope: 4-week PoC focusing on 1) latency and throughput validation, 2) model accuracy on 5 sample prompt families, and 3) security integration (SSO + KMS + audit logs).
- Timeline: Kickoff week of 3/8, baseline tests in week 1, integration and tuning week 2-3, verification + wrap-up week 4.
- Stakeholders: Acme — Sara (PM), Tom (Infra lead); Redwood — Ben (AM), Marissa (Solutions/eng).
- Success criteria (draft): P95 latency < 150ms for 95% of test runs, edge-case F1 within 3 points of baseline, full audit log delivery to Acme SIEM.

I've attached a first-pass PoC plan (PoC-plan-acme-v1.pdf) and a mutual action plan template. Can you confirm: 1) that the Private VPC preference is correct, 2) whether Tom can join a 30-min kickoff on 3/9 or 3/10, and 3) any procurement contacts I should loop in early?

If Private VPC is a must, we'll loop our Private deployment team for scoping (networking + compliance checklist) — Marissa, can you prep the baseline checklist?

Thanks,
Ben

--
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0198
From: Sara Lin <sara.lin@acmecorp.com>

Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 10:12:00 -0500

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few items from our side:
- Deployment preference: Private VPC (must) — we need VPC peering with strict CIDR blocks and ASA audit logs.
- Timeline: 6–8 weeks preferred for a full security review; 4-week engineering PoC is fine if we run security review in parallel.
- Success criteria (additions):
  * Latency P95 < 150ms (as you listed)
  * Throughput: sustain 250 RPS for 30 minutes during load test
  * Cost target: operational estimate under $X per 1k tokens (we'll provide current spend baseline)
  * Compliance: SOC 2 evidence and detailed audit logs delivered to our SIEM.

Tom (cc) will own infra/networking details. Tom — can your team provide the network contact & preferred maintenance window for testing?

Procurement: Looping Sarah Mehta (procurement@acmecorp.com) later this week once we agree on scope.

Attached: brief security checklist we discussed (network-security-requirements.docx).

Happy to do a 30-min kickoff on 3/10 at 10:00am ET if that works for Redwood.

—Sara
